headline: Neural and graph models recover finer spatial gene expression and tissue domains
label: Spatial Transcriptomics Computational Methods
summary: Recent methods target spot-level limits in spatial transcriptomics using histology fusion, graph learning, and implicit neural fields.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned representation of spatial transcriptomic data that encodes spatial neighborhood or histology context within the model to recover information lost at spot-level resolution. Resolution enhancement and cell-level deconvolution are represented by HiFi-ST's continuous expression fields, STRESS's state-space refinement onto finer grids, CPS's coordinate-network imputation, SpaBiT's histology-graph fusion, and DeSpaST's histology-guided deconvolution. Other entries address spatially variable gene detection (VISGP, smNSF, BatchSVG), spatial domain identification (AGCLD, MCFST, SGFST, SpaHNR), spatial RNA velocity (spaVelo), and cross-modality alignment (MGW, SIVA, Garfield). Adjacent work includes flow cytometry, 3D segmentation, and single-cell geometry. Not all items share this thread; the common element is explicit spatial or histological context.
